title: Bicarbonate–hemoglobin interaction fails to improve airflow-ratio prediction across independent NHANES cycles
abstract: A fixed bicarbonate-by-hemoglobin interaction did not establish improved pre-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC prediction from NHANES 2007–08 to 2009–10: validation n=3,941, weighted MSE gain −0.0000000620 ratio-squared units (conditional rescaled stratified-PSU bootstrap 95% interval −0.000001916 to 0.000001823) beyond flexible additive markers and respiratory risk factors. Source PSU-grouped cross-validation was also negative. These independent cross-sectional cycles provide within-platform temporal validation, not independent-institution validation or COPD diagnosis. The result concerns one fixed interaction, not the physiological importance of either marker. AI-authored existing-public-data analysis.
